self.disposition: 7-item checklist run, all pass/n-a, recorded in the iterate ADR's Self-Review section (.shipwright/planning/adr/iterate-2026-09-15-t8-run-build-preview-adopt-ac-bindings.md).

findings.finding: The new test `test_reload_context_states_which_phase_was_interrupted` targets the one state ("in_progress") that the existing suite demonstrably never exercised. That is precisely where latent bugs live — if `single_session_recovery.py` mishandles the interrupted state, this test turns the sub-iterate green-run assumption into a red CI and a scope expansion (fixing recovery logic inside a tagging change).
findings.suggestion: Run the new tests locally before claiming the bound; if they fail, that's a separate bug-fix iterate, not a tag — say so explicitly rather than absorbing the fix.  2. Category: risk — Severity: medium

findings.finding: Same pattern for `test_catalogue_followup.py` — `confirmation_triage` is described as "completely UNTESTED," so 3 new tests against never-executed code carry the same latent-failure risk, plus a naming risk: an untested function may not conform to what the AC's "tracked human follow-up" language expects.
findings.suggestion: Same as above: pre-run and pre-classify. Also confirm the 3 tests cover the AC02 handover-count clause, not just the function's happy path.  3. Category: approach — Severity: low

findings.finding: Counting FR-01.12 AC01's "spawn half" as bound (5/9) slightly overstates coverage — only half the AC is proven and the baseline will show it bound. The plan does disclose this, and Exception 1 mandates it, but the recorded reason in the baseline should say "half-bound, no-seam for precondition" rather than a plain bound tag.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the baseline entry (or its reason field) carries the half-bound annotation so downstream ratchet checks don't treat AC01 as fully proven.  4. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: test_complete_without_test_counts_is_rejected` assumes the section-builder schema contract is the only gate. If any other code path accepts a complete payload (e.g., a lenient parser elsewhere, or the section-state recording that "accepts any string"), the AC's "never declared done on unproven code" claim is only partially enforced and the negative test proves less than the AC.
findings.suggestion: Verify the schema validator is the sole enforcement point for completion; if a parallel lenient path exists, note it in the Exception 9 record for AC07 rather than implying full coverage.  5. Category: dependency — Severity: low

findings.finding: The two-step regeneration order (traceability collector first, then `check_ac_coverage_ratchet.py --write`) is load-bearing — regenerating the baseline from a stale `test-traceability.json` would silently undercount. The plan states the order but nothing enforces it.
findings.suggestion: Make the regen a single scripted step or at least assert post-regen that the unbound count matches the expected 18-bound/12-unbound split before finishing.  6. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: Leaving the regenerated baseline manifest uncommitted relies on CI rebuilding it from fresh JUnit output. If any of the five test roots produces a different tag set in CI (e.g., the adopt/dev_server files that were "simply untagged" get re-tagged only via the collector in some environment-specific way), the committed-vs-CI baseline can drift.
findings.suggestion: Spot-check CI's regen output once after merge and confirm the unbound delta matches the local 85 → 67 figure.  7. Category: approach — Severity: low (positive)

findings.finding: Rejecting the FR-01.05 proxy binding (section-state accepting any string as a commit) is the correct call and directly honors the "prove the AC" constraint. Exception 9 mirroring Exception 1 is consistent precedent.
findings.suggestion: None — keep the rejection rationale in the survey record, it's the right artifact for reviewers.  No security concerns: this is test-and-tag work with no production code paths touched beyond read access.  Overall assessment: This is a disciplined, well-evidenced tagging pass that correctly distinguishes tagging gaps from testing gaps and resists proxy-binding to inflate the count. The main watch items are the latent-failure risk in the three genuinely new tests against never-exercised code, and keeping the half-bound AC01 clearly annotated in the baseline.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: FR-01.12/AC01 is counted as bound although the plan explicitly says its “at least one build section is complete” precondition cannot be proved. A spawn/URL test proves only one half of a conjunctive AC.
findings.suggestion: Record AC01 as unbound/partial with the precondition’s no-seam reason, or add a seam that creates a completed build section and proves the server behavior under that state. Recalculate the totals accordingly (17 bound / 13 unbound if no other AC changes).

findings.finding: FR-01.05/AC07 is treated as proven by requiring `tests_passed` and `tests_total` fields on a `complete` payload. Required self-reported counts do not prove tests actually ran, passed, or apply to the delivered code.
findings.suggestion: Keep AC07 unbound unless the completion path consumes verified test-run evidence (for example, a result artifact or trusted runner output) and the test exercises rejection when that evidence is absent or failing.

findings.finding: The plan introduces “Exception 9, written this run” for `/shipwright-build`, while the binding constraint requires using the t0 seam-survey row rather than re-deciding a seam. The plan cites t0 for preview but does not establish that t0 already approved this new build exception.
findings.suggestion: Amend the t0 survey first, with the owner-accepted row and explicit AC-level reasons for FR-01.05, then cite that stable row in this iterate.

findings.finding: The new `catalogue_followup.confirmation_triage` tests appear unit-focused, but AC03 requires a human follow-up to be tracked. Testing an otherwise uncalled function’s return value would not prove the application creates and persists/escalates follow-up during the adoption workflow.
findings.suggestion: Include an integration-level assertion from the real adoption path through to the persisted/auditable follow-up record, alongside targeted unit cases for triage branches.

findings.finding: The execution plan does not name the exact pytest/JUnit invocations or reconcile roots. It names five surveyed roots, while the scope names four plugin test roots and the preview proof is actually in `shared/tests`. This leaves ADR-044 compliance and coverage collection reproducibility ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: State one concrete command and JUnit output path for each actual root, including `shared/tests` and any `shared/scripts/tests` invocation, and run the collector/ratchet against those outputs before finalizing the baseline.

findings.finding: “Uncommitted-but-present” traceability output risks a baseline that only passes locally. If CI regenerates from JUnit differently, the committed coverage baseline can drift or the new links may disappear.
findings.suggestion: Add a clean-worktree verification that runs the exact CI sequence and confirms regenerated traceability and baseline are identical to the intended checked-in coverage result (or explicitly commit the required source manifest if it is an input).  No new runtime security exposure is apparent from these test and traceability changes. The general reuse-first direction is sound, but the plan currently overstates two partial proofs and needs its seam-governance and CI regeneration details tightened before implementation.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.suggestion: Update the mini-plan's Result section and step 3 to match the ADR's final state (FR-01.05 0/8, 85→68, 17-of-30). A reviewer reading only the mini-plan gets a wrong coverage picture.  2. Category: test — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The diff uses the `covers` marker with multiple positional args in several places, but nothing in the diff shows the traceability collector (`test_links.py`) actually iterating `mark.args` rather than reading a single string. If the collector reads only one tag (or does `mark.args[0]`), the second AC silently loses its binding and the regenerated baseline would not match what the ADR's table claims. The newly registered marker description in `plugins/shipwright-build/pyproject.toml` says "one or more FRs", but that is documentation, not proof.
findings.suggestion: Verify (or show in the ADR) that `test_links.py` handles multi-arg `covers` markers; otherwise split into stacked single-arg decorators, which is the pattern used everywhere else in this diff.  3. Category: spec — Severity: low (contested, disclosed)

findings.finding: The sub-iterate's binding constraint says "cite the row t0 produced … rather than re-deciding the seam," yet Exception 9 for FR-01.05 was written by t8 itself mid-run. The ADR's rejection of openai's HIGH finding relies on precedent (Exceptions 5–8) rather than a t0 decision, so the letter of the binding constraint is not met even if the spirit is. Also, `FR-01.12/AC01` was removed from `unbound` while being only half-bound, and the baseline schema (per the ADR's own finding #9) cannot record "half-bound" — so the machine-readable artifact overstates the binding that only prose discloses.
findings.suggestion: Get explicit owner sign-off on Exception 9 retroactively (or note it as pending), and consider whether AC01's half-bind should stay in `unbound` until the schema can represent it, matching openai's recalculated 17/13 split.  4. Category: test — Severity: low

findings.finding: The assertions `"3" in card["title"]` / `"5" in card["detail"]` / `"as of onboarding" in card["detail"]` are substring checks that can pass on coincidental digit matches (e.g. a date, a count of a different field, or an FR-id fragment) and would survive wording drift that removes the semantic claim. The docstring-anchored `"as of onboarding"` assertion is a literal-string pin that breaks on any rewording without proving the snapshot semantics.
findings.suggestion: Assert the count against a computed expectation (e.g. a regex like `r"\b3 unconfirmed\b"` or parse the number out) rather than a bare substring, so the test proves the count is actually derived from the catalogue.  5. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: The new test uses `_done_task` and `_config_with` helpers and `json`/`reload_orchestrator_context` without visible imports/definitions in the diff hunk — presumably existing in the file, but the ADR's local-green claim is the only evidence the fixture shapes match production serialization (e.g. whether a real interrupted run writes `result: None` vs. omitting the key). If production omits `result` rather than writing `None`, the test would pass on a state production never produces.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the fixture shape matches what `update_step`/recovery actually persists for an interrupted phase (ideally by generating one via the real code path in the test, not a hand-written dict).  6. Category: regression — Severity: low

findings.finding: Decorative separator-comment removals were made purely to stay under a bloat cap (Self-Review item 6). While not a functional bug, the blank-line-before-class removals in `test_section_builder_contract.py` degrade readability for zero behavioral gain and are churn unrelated to the AC work; also the new `test_complete_without_test_counts_is_rejected` was added directly after a blank-line deletion, making the class boundary ambiguous in `TestInvalidPayloads`.
findings.suggestion: Skip cosmetic line-count games; if a file must be trimmed, trim dead weight, not visual structure.

findings.finding: FR-01.12/AC01` is removed from `unbound` even though its tagged test only proves server spawn/URL output and explicitly does not prove the AC’s required “at least one build section is complete” precondition. The coverage gate will therefore treat a conjunctive AC as fully proven.
findings.suggestion: Keep AC01 unbound/partial with the no-seam reason until a test can establish the completed-section precondition and exercise preview under that state.

findings.finding: The recorded test commands omit the required `--junitxml` argument for every exercised root. This violates the explicit ADR-044 constraint of one pytest invocation and one JUnit XML output per root, and leaves the claimed regenerated traceability evidence unreproducible.
findings.suggestion: Run and record one command per actual root with distinct `--junitxml` paths, then regenerate coverage from those outputs.

findings.finding: The final accounting claims “18 of 30 ACs bound” and “12” unbound, but the committed baseline changes from 85 to 68 unbound: only 17 entries were removed. Moreover, one of those 17 is the partial FR-01.12/AC01 binding, while FR-01.05/AC07 is explicitly retracted. The evidence artifacts therefore overstate coverage.
findings.suggestion: Correct the plan/ADR totals to match the baseline and distinguish fully proven, partial, and unbound ACs.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The change contains useful test bindings, but it currently marks a partially proven AC as complete and does not meet the required JUnit execution evidence.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
